gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-meetei-mayek: Styro packs its retro letters so tightly they nearly touch, with barely any gap in the e. Noto Sans Meetei Mayek lets its large, cracked-bangle rounds breathe, so a longer passage moves along easily.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-mende-kikakui: Commanding and retro, Styro crowds its letters together until the counters nearly vanish. And Noto Sans Mende Kikakui lets daylight through every curve, its tall lowercase giving the heading room to bark.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-meroitic: Styro's pressed-together letters give it a retro, commanding punch, with e and c shapes that almost seal shut. Noto Sans Meroitic simply stays open and readable.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-modi: Noto Sans Modi reads clean and modern, with daylight inside every curve and lowercase close to capital height. Styro, by contrast, is the tight, retro counterweight, its closed letters making the open sans-serif feel even lighter.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-mono: Tight, retro and loud. Styro crowds its letters, while Noto Sans Mono spaces its sturdy, tall lowercase generously, so the heading hits hard and the text underneath stays open.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-mro: Styro brings a retro, commanding look, its letters crammed together with hardly a gap left in the e or c. Noto Sans Mro answers with wide entrances into each letter.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-multani: Noto Sans Multani reads modern and lofty, its e opening wide at the terminal and its x-height standing high. Styro does the shouting, crowded and retro; the sans-serif does the talking.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Styro delivers retro command, its crowded letters barely leaving room inside the e or c. Noto Sans Myanmar forms a heavy-looking band of text with a broad, welcoming c, handling the reading while the heading makes the entrance.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Styro is retro and commanding, its letters pressed so close that the e and c almost close up. Noto Sans Nabataean stands nearly cap-tall with wide s curves, giving the sans-serif text real openness against the heading's tightness.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-nag-mundari: Noto Sans Nag Mundari looks half unwrapped, with open c and s shapes. Styro sits against it with crowded, retro letters, while the plain sans lowercase rivals the capitals in height and keeps the text confident.
